meta.title: Questions engineered into capability.
meta.description: Labs is where NEXUS investigates technologies before they become system decisions. Every track begins with a practical question, follows an explicit method and produces knowledge that can be transferred into real projects.

featured.title: Intelligence deserves an engineering discipline.
featured.description: The primary investigation explores how intelligent features can be designed, evaluated and operated as dependable parts of a larger software system.
featured.question: How can an AI capability remain useful, measurable and transparent after the first successful prototype?
featured.hypothesis: Reliable intelligent systems emerge when evaluation, data quality and operational constraints are treated as architecture—not final checks.

protocol.name: Frame
protocol.description: Turn a broad technology interest into a precise engineering question.

protocol.name: Prototype
protocol.description: Build the smallest artifact capable of testing the central assumption.

protocol.name: Measure
protocol.description: Record evidence, failure modes and the limits of the result.

protocol.name: Transfer
protocol.description: Convert validated learning into a reusable system capability.

registry.title: Five disciplines, one engineering ecosystem.
registry.description: Each track has a distinct research surface, but the value appears when insights move across boundaries—from backend and cloud foundations to data, security and intelligent behavior.

tracks.name: Artificial Intelligence
tracks.description: Applied intelligence, evaluation strategies and the software boundaries required to make model-driven behavior dependable.
tracks.question: How should intelligent features be evaluated before they become system dependencies?
tracks.transfer: Future intelligent layers for NGDP and other NEXUS systems.

tracks.name: Cloud Computing
tracks.description: Architecture, delivery and observability patterns for systems that must remain understandable while they scale.
tracks.question: Which platform decisions improve reliability without creating unnecessary operational complexity?
tracks.transfer: Deployment foundations and operating models for project workloads.

tracks.name: Cybersecurity
tracks.description: Security principles embedded into identity, data handling and platform design from the beginning of a system.
tracks.question: How can secure defaults become part of architecture instead of a later correction?
tracks.transfer: Trust boundaries and defensive practices across the ecosystem.

tracks.name: Data Engineering
tracks.description: Traceable pipelines, explicit quality decisions and data products that remain useful beyond a single analysis.
tracks.question: What makes a small data pipeline dependable enough to evolve into a platform?
tracks.transfer: Pipeline practices applied directly to NGDP and HEVY.

tracks.name: Backend Engineering
tracks.description: Software boundaries, interfaces and testing practices that give every higher-level capability a durable foundation.
tracks.question: Which abstractions keep a system simple today without limiting its next stage?
tracks.transfer: Reusable service patterns and dependable system interfaces.

principle.title: Evidence before expansion.
principle.description: A lab result is not a promise of production readiness. It is a documented reduction in uncertainty: what was tested, what was learned, where it failed and what deserves to move forward.
outcomes: A clear transfer or stop decision
